# United States Emigration and Immigration

The United States has been a destination for immigrants since colonial times. Genealogical records of immigration exist from the 1600s onward, with systematic federal passenger record-keeping beginning in 1820.

## Customs Passenger Lists (1820–1891)

The Steerage Act of 1819 (effective 1820) required ship captains to file a passenger manifest with U.S. Customs upon arrival. These lists are the primary federal source for immigration records from 1820 through 1891.

### What the Lists Record

Customs Passenger Lists name **every passenger aboard the vessel** — adults, children, and infants traveling with a family group. Each entry typically includes:

- Full name
- Age
- Sex
- Occupation (for adults)
- Country of origin

Because all passengers are listed individually, a researcher examining a manifest for one adult immigrant should read the **entire page** to identify accompanying family members — spouses, children of all ages, and siblings who traveled together. Young children and infants are listed by name alongside the head of household.

### Coverage and Access

Customs lists cover arrivals at major U.S. ports (New York, Boston, Philadelphia, Baltimore, New Orleans, and others). The lists for New York (Castle Garden, 1820–1892) are the most extensive. FamilySearch has indexed and digitized much of this collection.

## Immigration and Naturalization Service Records (1891–present)

Federal immigration inspection shifted from Customs to the Bureau of Immigration in 1891. Ellis Island (New York) processed the majority of arrivals from 1892 to 1954. Post-1906 naturalization records are held by USCIS and the National Archives.

## Key Research Strategies

- Identify the port of departure as well as arrival — Irish Famine emigrants (1845–1852) primarily arrived through New York (Castle Garden), Philadelphia, or Boston.
- Pull the full manifest page, not just the indexed entry, to locate traveling companions.
- Check both the passenger lists and the port health records — cholera and typhus outbreaks during the Famine years generated supplementary documentation.
- For Irish immigrants before 1895, Castle Garden records (1820–1892) predate Ellis Island and cover the Famine period entirely.
